phrase.text: parameter is another name for the caller's variable: whatever the subprogram does to it, it does to that variable.

runs.text: parameter is another name for the caller's variable: whatever the subprogram does to it, it does to that variable.
Since the subprogram receives a variable and not a value, the argument must be a
: a variable, a cell or an attribute. A literal or an operation will not do.

runs.text: had no value before the call, and that is not an error: the engine sees that
on every path. Those parameters are
parameters. If the subprogram read the parameter before assigning it, the argument would have to arrive with a value.

entries.text: The index of a cell passed by reference is computed only once, at the call. An invalid index fails before entering the subprogram.
Two parameters may refer to the same variable; it is not forbidden.
In recursive subprograms no parameter counts as an output parameter.

blocks.title: A literal by reference

diagnostics.message: An argument passed by reference must be a variable or array element

points.text: The argument must be a designator of the exact type.
It is used to return several results.
If the subprogram assigns before reading, the argument may arrive without a value.
